A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SageAttention2 work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.9 support a complete comparison; bibliography expansion and text reflow explain the additional page in v7.

before.justification: V5 reports original kernel benchmarks, end-to-end evaluations, ablations, and qualitative generation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V7 retains these original empirical results, including additional language, image, video, long-context, and speech-recognition evaluations in Appendix A.9.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects two stated update steps: it restores the previous softmax normalizer factor and removes an erroneous inverse from output rescaling. These corrections align the pseudocode with Equation 1 and Section 3.4 already in v5. The quantization design is unchanged, and an evaluated implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same language, image/video generation, image classification, speech-recognition, and long-context tasks. Appendices A.7–A.9 retain the same datasets and scenarios; newly cited diffusion work does not introduce evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding comparisons, including HadmdAttn, SmoothAttn, SageAttention, and FlashAttention3(fp8) where evaluated. The new sparse-attention citations are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, model configurations, and testing procedures are retained. Appendix A.8 still specifies batch size 4, 32 attention heads, head dimensions 64 and 128, causal/noncausal evaluation, and the same input-generation distributions.

E4.justification: The smoothing, quantization-granularity, numerical-format, overhead, and long-context analyses are unchanged, including Tables 4–7, 10, and 15–19. Appendix A.4 adds an interpretation of smoothing V, without adding an ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and layer-average/worst-layer summaries. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged. Table 8 retains CogvideoX (1.5-5B) latencies of 1040, 577, and 555 seconds for original, 8-bit, and 4-bit attention. Table 10 retains cosine similarities of 98.25% without and 99.75% with smoothing V.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 repairs mathematically non-equivalent recurrences: the normalizer update gains the missing previous-normalizer multiplier, and output rescaling loses its incorrect inverse. Equation 1, the Gaussian smoothing analysis in Appendix A.5, and the per-thread formulation in A.6 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims: per-thread quantization, smoothing Q, two-level accumulation, approximately 3x/4.5x speedups over FlashAttention2/xformers, and comparable Hopper speed with higher accuracy than FlashAttention3(fp8).

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 expands its CogvideoX-specific discussion by stating that smoothing V is generally effective for diffusion models. This broadens the applicability interpretation without additional experiments. The existing qualification that benefits depend on channel-wise bias remains.

D1.justification: The code-access information, CUDA kernel descriptions, GPU constraints, warp/block details in Appendix A.6, and benchmark input-generation instructions in A.8 are retained. No additional implementation settings or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: V7 adds two sparse-video-attention references in the introduction and seven diffusion-related references in Appendix A.4, including DPM-Solver-v3, RIFLEx, and FrameBridge. These extend citation coverage without substantially revising the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Changes are limited to the added Appendix A.4 sentence, citation edits, bibliographic metadata updates, and version/date text. The main narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The bibliography starts beneath the impact statement in v7 rather than in the next column, reflows, and ends on a mostly empty page. Some appendix text breaks shift. All 20 figures and 20 tables retain their display structures and visual content.

improvement.justification: Correcting Algorithm 1 resolves two consequential inconsistencies with equations already present in v5, improving the reliability of the pseudocode. The broader diffusion-model assertion is not accompanied by additional experimental support, limiting its added value. With empirical evidence and method design otherwise stable, the overall improvement is modest.
